blocks.headline: Driving growth and clinical value with data-driven care.
blocks.subtitle: How Right at Home Tri-County Metro uses Able Assess to close the "assessment gap" — winning more assessments and converting more inquiries into clients.

blocks.body:
Jeff Welsh, the owner of Right at Home Tri-County Metro, is an innovative leader who bridges the gap between compassionate care and clinical precision. By integrating technology like Able Assess, he has built his agency into a forward-thinking organization that delivers measurable results, moving beyond traditional, static care models to focus on longevity and independence.

Bridging the assessment gap

One of the most pressing challenges Jeff identified within his operations was the “assessment gap” — the friction point between a family’s initial inquiry and the actual in-home evaluation. Jeff noted that while his team is exceptional at fielding calls, only about a third of those inquiries typically transition to the next step.

To bridge this, Jeff integrated Able Assess as a cornerstone of his sales strategy, viewing the technology as a way to offer immediate, hospital-grade value before a contract is even signed. By promising a free, sophisticated fall-risk screening, Jeff believes he can push his assessment conversion rate from 40% to a target of 60%. For Jeff, this isn’t just about the math; it’s about providing families with objective insight that offers instant clarity during a high-stress decision-making process.

So now if a prospect is calling for answers about home care, maybe they’re going to talk to three of them to decide who’s going to come to the house. I give them an advantage with Able Assess. I think it’s going to increase the likelihood that I will get a chance to make that assessment and change that metric. Our numbers show that if we get to that assessment, the chances of converting the caller to an actual client are actually very good.

Strengthening the healthcare ecosystem

Beyond the initial sale, Jeff’s vision extends to the entire healthcare ecosystem. He recognizes that home care should not exist in a vacuum, and he uses the data generated by Able Assess to transform his agency into a vital clinical partner for primary care physicians and skilled therapy providers.

When Jeff’s team identifies a decline in a client’s grip strength or gait speed through the Able Assess portal, they proactively reach out to primary care physicians and physical therapists. This data-driven advocacy allows healthcare partners to “swoop in” with the necessary interventions, creating a reciprocal relationship built on professional trust. This approach has turned his agency into a facilitator of wider care, ensuring that his clients are safer while his professional partners view Right at Home as a sophisticated, essential ally.

Making referrals to trusted skilled therapy providers increases your value to your professional healthcare partners when you see signs of weakness and potential for falls.

Redefining market differentiation

This commitment to differentiation is most visible in how Jeff handles community outreach. Rather than standard marketing, Jeff utilizes group screenings at independent and assisted living communities as a powerful reason for engagement. These events allow him to offer a genuine service to residents while simultaneously building a pipeline of prospective clients who now see Right at Home as an expert in fall prevention.

By focusing on the “why” — the simplicity, speed and immense value of the information — Jeff has moved his business beyond the traditional model of “selling hours.” Instead, he is selling a holistic care plan backed by trend data and objective proof, ensuring that every client under his care isn’t just being watched, but is actually getting stronger.

A future-focused mission

Ultimately, Jeff Welsh’s adoption of Able Assess is a natural extension of his mission to be a “navigator” for families facing the complexities of aging. As he continues to scale these innovations across the Tri-County Metro area, Jeff remains focused on the one outcome that truly matters: helping seniors stay safe, independent, and exactly where they want to be — at home.
